109	# --- Ingredient scaling -----------------------------------------------------

111	_UNICODE_FRACTIONS = "¼-¾⅐-⅞"  # ¼ ½ ¾ ⅐ … ⅞

113	_RANGE_SEP = r"(?:[-–—~]|to\b|or\b)"  # "-", "–", "—", "~", "to", "or"

116	# or integer/decimal ("200", "1.5", ".5"). Longest forms are tried first, so
117	# the US-style "1-1/2" is read as one-and-a-half, not as the range 1 to 1/2.

119	    rf"(?:\d+(?:\s+|-)\d+{_SLASH}\d+"
120	    rf"|\d+\s*[{_UNICODE_FRACTIONS}]"
121	    rf"|\d+{_SLASH}\d+"
122	    rf"|[{_UNICODE_FRACTIONS}]"
123	    r"|\d+(?:\.\d+)?|\.\d+)"
124	)
125	
126	# A leading quantity, optionally a range ("1-2", "1 to 2", "2 or 3").
127	_QUANTITY_RE = re.compile(
128	    r"^(?P<lead>\s*)"
129	    rf"(?P<low>{_NUMBER})"
130	    rf"(?:(?P<sep>\s*{_RANGE_SEP}\s*)(?P<high>{_NUMBER}))?"
131	    r"(?![\d/⁄.])",  # don't stop mid-token (e.g. "1.2.3", "1/2/3")
132	    # ASCII: \d is only 0-9 here. Other scripts' digits ("٢ cups") aren't read
133	    # as a quantity, so _ANY_NUMBER_RE (Unicode \d) reports them as unscaled.
134	    re.IGNORECASE | re.ASCII,
135	)
136	# Longer quantities are not real recipe amounts; refusing them also keeps us
137	# clear of Python 3.11+'s 4300-digit int<->str limit (ValueError -> HTTP 500).
138	_MAX_QUANTITY_DIGITS = 100
139	
140	# General rule: a digit or fraction anywhere that is not part of the supported
141	# leading quantity is a number we don't understand – after it ("1 lb 4 oz",
142	# "12 oz (340 g)", "1,5 kg", "2x3 cm") or with no readable leading quantity
143	# at all ("flour 200 g", "Eggs: 2", "~2 cups", "1.2.3", "-2 g"). Such lines are
144	# reported instead of being scaled wrongly or passed off as "no quantity".
145	_ANY_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(rf"[\d{_UNICODE_FRACTIONS}]")
146	
147	# The same rule for numbers written as words: "two eggs", "half a lemon",
148	# "2 cups plus one tbsp". Like a stray digit, a number word anywhere means the
149	# line may hold an amount we can't scale, so it is reported. Accepted cost:
150	# "half-and-half" (the dairy product) and "cut in half" are reported too.
151	_NUMBER_WORD_RE = re.compile(
152	    r"\b(?:one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|eleven|twelve"
153	    r"|dozens?|couple|half|halves|quarters?|thirds?)\b",
154	    re.IGNORECASE,
155	)
156	
157	# A unit followed by a container describes the container's size, not an
158	# amount: "2 inch piece", "3 ounce can", "1 lb bag", "400 g tin".
159	_SIZE_UNIT = (
160	    r"(?:inch(?:es)?|in|cm|mm|ounces?|oz|pounds?|lbs?|g|grams?|kg"
161	    r"|ml|l|lit(?:er|re)s?)"
162	)
163	_CONTAINER = (
164	    r"(?:pieces?|cans?|tins?|jars?|bags?|box(?:es)?|packages?|packets?|pkgs?"
165	    r"|blocks?|bottles?|cartons?|sticks?|chunks?|containers?|tubs?|slices?)"
166	)
167	
168	# The leading number is there but is not an amount of the ingredient.
169	_NOT_AN_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(
170	    r"^(?:"
171	    r"[-–]\s*[^\W\d_]"                              # size: "2-inch piece", "3-ounce can"
172	    rf"|\s+{_SIZE_UNIT}\s+{_CONTAINER}\b"           # size: "2 inch piece", "3 ounce can"
173	    r"|\s*(?:[%°]|percent\b|per\s+cent\b|degrees?\b)"  # "70% / 70 percent", "180°C / degrees"

175	    re.IGNORECASE,

179	_FRACTION_RE = re.compile(rf"(\d+){_SLASH}(\d+)")

184	    """Exact value of one _NUMBER token, or None if it is invalid ("1/0")."""
185	    m = _MIXED_RE.fullmatch(text)
186	    if m:
187	        whole, num, den = map(int, m.groups())
188	        # A real mixed number has a proper fraction part. "1-3/2" could just as
189	        # well be the range 1 to 3/2, so improper parts are rejected as ambiguous.
190	        return whole + Fraction(num, den) if 0 < den and num < den else None
191	    m = _FRACTION_RE.fullmatch(text)
192	    if m:
193	        num, den = map(int, m.groups())
194	        return Fraction(num, den) if den else None
195	    m = _UNICODE_MIXED_RE.fullmatch(text)
196	    if m:
197	        # unicodedata gives a float (⅓ -> 0.333…); every vulgar fraction has den <= 10.
198	        frac = Fraction(unicodedata.numeric(m[2])).limit_denominator(10)
199	        return int(m[1] or 0) + frac
200	    return Fraction(text)

203	def _format_quantity(value: Fraction) -> str:
204	    """Render a non-negative quantity without trailing zeros.
205	
206	    One rule: keep at least 2 decimal places, and for values below 1 keep
207	    2 significant digits, so small amounts never collapse or double:
208	
209	        2 -> "2"      1/2 -> "0.5"     1/3 -> "0.33"    10/3 -> "3.33"
210	        0.005 -> "0.005"   0.0123 -> "0.012"   0.995 -> "1"
211	    """
212	    if value.denominator == 1:
213	        return str(value.numerator)
214	    with localcontext() as ctx:
215	        # Enough precision for any input size: the default 28 digits makes
216	        # quantize() raise InvalidOperation on huge amounts (HTTP 500).
217	        int_digits = len(str(value.numerator // value.denominator))
218	        ctx.prec = max(28, int_digits + 2 * len(str(value.denominator)) + 10)

220	        # adjusted() is the exponent of the leading digit: 0.005 -> -3, 3.3 -> 0.
221	        places = max(2, 1 - exact.adjusted())
222	        rounded = exact.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)

224	    return text.rstrip("0").rstrip(".") if "." in text else text

229	
230	    Supported leading quantities (scaled, x2 shown):
231	      integer/decimal  "200 g" -> "400 g", "1.5 tsp" -> "3 tsp", ".5 cup" -> "1 cup"
232	      fraction         "1/2 cup" -> "1 cup", "1⁄2 cup" -> "1 cup", "½ cup" -> "1 cup"
233	      mixed number     "1 1/2", "1-1/2", "1½", "1 ½" -> "3"
234	      range            "1-2" -> "2-4", "1 to 2" -> "2 to 4", "2 or 3" -> "4 or 6"
235	
236	    Returns:
237	      * the scaled line;
238	      * the line unchanged if it contains no digits, fractions or number
239	        words at all ("salt to taste", "a pinch of nutmeg");
240	      * None if it can't be scaled safely. The caller reports these in
241	        "unscaled" instead of returning a wrong amount. Accepted limitations:
242	          - quantity not at the start: "flour 200 g", "Eggs: 2",
243	            "a 400 g can tomatoes", "about 2 cups", "~2 cups", "V8 juice"
244	          - another number after the quantity: "1 lb 4 oz beef",
245	            "1 cup plus 2 tbsp", "3 eggs or 4 egg whites", "12 oz (340 g)",
246	            "2 x 400 g cans", "2x3 cm", "1 2-inch piece", "1-2-3 eggs",
247	            "2 eggs, beaten in 1 bowl", "2 cans V8 juice"
248	          - number words anywhere: "two eggs", "half a lemon",
249	            "2 cups plus one tbsp", and as a side effect "1 cup half-and-half",
250	            "1 lemon, cut in half"
251	          - decimal comma / thousands separator: "1,5 kg", "1,000 g"
252	          - not an amount (a size, percentage or temperature): "2-inch piece",
253	            "2 inch piece", "3-ounce can", "3 ounce can", "1 lb bag",
254	            "70% cocoa", "70 percent cocoa", "180°C", "180 degrees"
255	          - digits in other scripts: "٢ cups"
256	          - unreadable / invalid: "1.2.3 cups", "1/2/3", "1e3 g", "1/0 cup",
257	            "-2 g", reversed range "2-1 cups", improper mixed number
258	            "1-3/2" (range or 2 1/2?), more than 100 digits
259	
260	    Ambiguous hyphens with a proper fraction are read as mixed numbers:
261	    "2-3/4" is 2 3/4, not the range 2 to 3/4. Results keep 2 decimals
262	    (2 significant digits below 1), so "1/8 tsp" becomes "0.13 tsp" even at
263	    factor 1.
264	    """
265	    if _NUMBER_WORD_RE.search(ingredient):
266	        return None
267	    match = _QUANTITY_RE.match(ingredient)
268	    if match is None:
269	        # No readable leading quantity: fine only if there's no number at all.
270	        return None if _ANY_NUMBER_RE.search(ingredient) else ingredient
271	    if sum(c.isdigit() for c in match.group()) > _MAX_QUANTITY_DIGITS:
272	        return None
273	    rest = ingredient[match.end():]
274	    if _ANY_NUMBER_RE.search(rest) or _NOT_AN_AMOUNT_RE.match(rest):
275	        return None
276	    low = _parse_number(match["low"])
277	    high = _parse_number(match["high"]) if match["high"] else None
278	    if low is None or (match["high"] and high is None):
279	        return None
280	    if high is not None and not low < high:
281	        return None  # "2-1 cups" is not a meaningful range
282	    scaled = _format_quantity(low * factor)
283	    if high is not None:
284	        scaled += match["sep"] + _format_quantity(high * factor)
285	    return match["lead"] + scaled + rest
286	
287	
288	def _json_number(value: Fraction) -> Union[int, float]:
289	    """2 -> 2, 1/2 -> 0.5: no trailing ".0" in the JSON response."""
290	    return value.numerator if value.denominator == 1 else float(value)
291	
292	
293	@app.get("/recipes/{recipe_id}/scaled")
294	def get_scaled_recipe(
295	    recipe_id: int,
296	    # Decimal, not float: the bounds are checked on the exact value, so
297	    # "10.0000000000000001" is rejected instead of rounding to 10.0.
298	    # max_digits bounds the work for inputs like "1e-999999" (still allows 1e-300).
299	    factor: Decimal = Query(..., gt=0, le=10, allow_inf_nan=False, max_digits=400),
300	):
301	    """Recipe with ingredient quantities multiplied by `factor` (0 < factor <= 10).
302	
303	    `unscaled` lists ingredient lines that start with a quantity but were left
304	    as-is because the amount is ambiguous. Lines without any quantity
305	    ("salt to taste") are unchanged by design and are not listed.
306	    """
307	    recipe = _fetch_recipe(recipe_id)
308	    exact_factor = Fraction(factor)  # Decimal -> Fraction is exact: "0.1" is 1/10
309	    ingredients, unscaled = [], []
310	    # No special case for factor == 1: output format must not depend on the
311	    # factor ("2.0 cups" -> "2 cups" and "1/3" -> "0.33" for every factor).
312	    for line in recipe["ingredients"]:
313	        scaled = scale_ingredient(line, exact_factor)
314	        if scaled is None:
315	            unscaled.append(line)
316	            scaled = line
317	        ingredients.append(scaled)
318	    return {
319	        **recipe,
320	        "factor": _json_number(exact_factor),
321	        "ingredients": ingredients,
322	        "unscaled": unscaled,
323	    }

"""Recipe Box — starter app for Week 7.

A tiny FastAPI service for recipes and tags, with a static frontend. Use it as the
playground for concurrent multi-agent work and a generator-critic loop.

Run:
    pip install -r requirements.txt
    uvicorn main:app --reload
    # open http://localhost:8000/
Test:
    pytest
"""
import json
import os
import re
import sqlite3
import unicodedata
from contextlib import closing
from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, localcontext
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Union

from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException, Query
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel

BASE = Path(__file__).parent
# Overridable so tests (or deployments) can point at a different database file.
DB_PATH = Path(os.environ.get("RECIPE_BOX_DB", BASE / "recipes.db"))

app = FastAPI(title="Recipe Box")


def get_db() -> sqlite3.Connection:
    conn = sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    return conn


def init_db() -> None:
    with closing(get_db()) as conn:
        conn.execute(
            """CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recipes (
                id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                title       TEXT NOT NULL,
                ingredients TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON list of strings
                tags        TEXT NOT NULL   -- JSON list of strings
            )"""
        )
        conn.commit()


init_db()


class RecipeIn(BaseModel):
    title: str
    ingredients: list[str] = []
    tags: list[str] = []


def _row_to_recipe(row: sqlite3.Row) -> dict:
    return {
        "id": row["id"],
        "title": row["title"],
        "ingredients": json.loads(row["ingredients"]),
        "tags": json.loads(row["tags"]),
    }


def _fetch_recipe(recipe_id: int) -> dict:
    with closing(get_db()) as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM recipes WHERE id = ?", (recipe_id,)).fetchone()
    if row is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="unknown recipe")
    return _row_to_recipe(row)


@app.get("/")
def index():
    return FileResponse(BASE / "static" / "index.html")


@app.post("/recipes")
def create_recipe(recipe: RecipeIn):
    with closing(get_db()) as conn:
        cur = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO recipes (title, ingredients, tags) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
            (recipe.title, json.dumps(recipe.ingredients), json.dumps(recipe.tags)),
        )
        conn.commit()
        rid = cur.lastrowid
    return {"id": rid, **recipe.model_dump()}


@app.get("/recipes")
def list_recipes():
    with closing(get_db()) as conn:
        rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM recipes ORDER BY id").fetchall()
    return [_row_to_recipe(r) for r in rows]


@app.get("/recipes/{recipe_id}")
def get_recipe(recipe_id: int):
    return _fetch_recipe(recipe_id)


# --- Ingredient scaling -----------------------------------------------------

_UNICODE_FRACTIONS = "¼-¾⅐-⅞"  # ¼ ½ ¾ ⅐ … ⅞
_SLASH = "[/⁄]"  # ASCII "/" or the Unicode fraction slash "⁄"
_RANGE_SEP = r"(?:[-–—~]|to\b|or\b)"  # "-", "–", "—", "~", "to", "or"

# One number: mixed ("1 1/2", "1-1/2", "1½", "1 ½"), fraction ("1/2", "½"),
# or integer/decimal ("200", "1.5", ".5"). Longest forms are tried first, so
# the US-style "1-1/2" is read as one-and-a-half, not as the range 1 to 1/2.
_NUMBER = (
    rf"(?:\d+(?:\s+|-)\d+{_SLASH}\d+"
    rf"|\d+\s*[{_UNICODE_FRACTIONS}]"
    rf"|\d+{_SLASH}\d+"
    rf"|[{_UNICODE_FRACTIONS}]"
    r"|\d+(?:\.\d+)?|\.\d+)"
)

# A leading quantity, optionally a range ("1-2", "1 to 2", "2 or 3").
_QUANTITY_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?P<lead>\s*)"
    rf"(?P<low>{_NUMBER})"
    rf"(?:(?P<sep>\s*{_RANGE_SEP}\s*)(?P<high>{_NUMBER}))?"
    r"(?![\d/⁄.])",  # don't stop mid-token (e.g. "1.2.3", "1/2/3")
    # ASCII: \d is only 0-9 here. Other scripts' digits ("٢ cups") aren't read
    # as a quantity, so _ANY_NUMBER_RE (Unicode \d) reports them as unscaled.
    re.IGNORECASE | re.ASCII,
)
# Longer quantities are not real recipe amounts; refusing them also keeps us
# clear of Python 3.11+'s 4300-digit int<->str limit (ValueError -> HTTP 500).
_MAX_QUANTITY_DIGITS = 100

# General rule: a digit or fraction anywhere that is not part of the supported
# leading quantity is a number we don't understand – after it ("1 lb 4 oz",
# "12 oz (340 g)", "1,5 kg", "2x3 cm") or with no readable leading quantity
# at all ("flour 200 g", "Eggs: 2", "~2 cups", "1.2.3", "-2 g"). Such lines are
# reported instead of being scaled wrongly or passed off as "no quantity".
_ANY_NUMBER_RE = re.compile(rf"[\d{_UNICODE_FRACTIONS}]")

# The same rule for numbers written as words: "two eggs", "half a lemon",
# "2 cups plus one tbsp". Like a stray digit, a number word anywhere means the
# line may hold an amount we can't scale, so it is reported. Accepted cost:
# "half-and-half" (the dairy product) and "cut in half" are reported too.
_NUMBER_WORD_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:one|two|three|four|five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten|eleven|twelve"
    r"|dozens?|couple|half|halves|quarters?|thirds?)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# A unit followed by a container describes the container's size, not an
# amount: "2 inch piece", "3 ounce can", "1 lb bag", "400 g tin".
_SIZE_UNIT = (
    r"(?:inch(?:es)?|in|cm|mm|ounces?|oz|pounds?|lbs?|g|grams?|kg"
    r"|ml|l|lit(?:er|re)s?)"
)
_CONTAINER = (
    r"(?:pieces?|cans?|tins?|jars?|bags?|box(?:es)?|packages?|packets?|pkgs?"
    r"|blocks?|bottles?|cartons?|sticks?|chunks?|containers?|tubs?|slices?)"
)

# The leading number is there but is not an amount of the ingredient.
_NOT_AN_AMOUNT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?:"
    r"[-–]\s*[^\W\d_]"                              # size: "2-inch piece", "3-ounce can"
    rf"|\s+{_SIZE_UNIT}\s+{_CONTAINER}\b"           # size: "2 inch piece", "3 ounce can"
    r"|\s*(?:[%°]|percent\b|per\s+cent\b|degrees?\b)"  # "70% / 70 percent", "180°C / degrees"
    r")",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

_MIXED_RE = re.compile(rf"(\d+)(?:\s+|-)(\d+){_SLASH}(\d+)")
_FRACTION_RE = re.compile(rf"(\d+){_SLASH}(\d+)")
_UNICODE_MIXED_RE = re.compile(rf"(\d*)\s*([{_UNICODE_FRACTIONS}])")


def _parse_number(text: str) -> Optional[Fraction]:
    """Exact value of one _NUMBER token, or None if it is invalid ("1/0")."""
    m = _MIXED_RE.fullmatch(text)
    if m:
        whole, num, den = map(int, m.groups())
        # A real mixed number has a proper fraction part. "1-3/2" could just as
        # well be the range 1 to 3/2, so improper parts are rejected as ambiguous.
        return whole + Fraction(num, den) if 0 < den and num < den else None

    if m:

        frac = Fraction(unicodedata.numeric(m[2])).limit_denominator(10)
        return int(m[1] or 0) + frac
    return Fraction(text)


def _format_quantity(value: Fraction) -> str:
    """Render a non-negative quantity without trailing zeros.

    One rule: keep at least 2 decimal places, and for values below 1 keep
    2 significant digits, so small amounts never collapse or double:

        2 -> "2"      1/2 -> "0.5"     1/3 -> "0.33"    10/3 -> "3.33"
        0.005 -> "0.005"   0.0123 -> "0.012"   0.995 -> "1"
    """
    if value.denominator == 1:
        return str(value.numerator)
    with localcontext() as ctx:
        # Enough precision for any input size: the default 28 digits makes
        # quantize() raise InvalidOperation on huge amounts (HTTP 500).
        int_digits = len(str(value.numerator // value.denominator))
        ctx.prec = max(28, int_digits + 2 * len(str(value.denominator)) + 10)
        exact = Decimal(value.numerator) / Decimal(value.denominator)
        # adjusted() is the exponent of the leading digit: 0.005 -> -3, 3.3 -> 0.
        places = max(2, 1 - exact.adjusted())
        rounded = exact.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    text = format(rounded, "f")
    return text.rstrip("0").rstrip(".") if "." in text else text


def scale_ingredient(ingredient: str, factor: Fraction) -> Optional[str]:
    """Scale the leading quantity (or range) of an ingredient line.

    Supported leading quantities (scaled, x2 shown):
      integer/decimal  "200 g" -> "400 g", "1.5 tsp" -> "3 tsp", ".5 cup" -> "1 cup"
      fraction         "1/2 cup" -> "1 cup", "1⁄2 cup" -> "1 cup", "½ cup" -> "1 cup"
      mixed number     "1 1/2", "1-1/2", "1½", "1 ½" -> "3"
      range            "1-2" -> "2-4", "1 to 2" -> "2 to 4", "2 or 3" -> "4 or 6"

    Returns:
      * the scaled line;
      * the line unchanged if it contains no digits, fractions or number
        words at all ("salt to taste", "a pinch of nutmeg");
      * None if it can't be scaled safely. The caller reports these in
        "unscaled" instead of returning a wrong amount. Accepted limitations:
          - quantity not at the start: "flour 200 g", "Eggs: 2",
            "a 400 g can tomatoes", "about 2 cups", "~2 cups", "V8 juice"
          - another number after the quantity: "1 lb 4 oz beef",
            "1 cup plus 2 tbsp", "3 eggs or 4 egg whites", "12 oz (340 g)",
            "2 x 400 g cans", "2x3 cm", "1 2-inch piece", "1-2-3 eggs",
            "2 eggs, beaten in 1 bowl", "2 cans V8 juice"
          - number words anywhere: "two eggs", "half a lemon",
            "2 cups plus one tbsp", and as a side effect "1 cup half-and-half",
            "1 lemon, cut in half"
          - decimal comma / thousands separator: "1,5 kg", "1,000 g"
          - not an amount (a size, percentage or temperature): "2-inch piece",
            "2 inch piece", "3-ounce can", "3 ounce can", "1 lb bag",
            "70% cocoa", "70 percent cocoa", "180°C", "180 degrees"
          - digits in other scripts: "٢ cups"
          - unreadable / invalid: "1.2.3 cups", "1/2/3", "1e3 g", "1/0 cup",
            "-2 g", reversed range "2-1 cups", improper mixed number
            "1-3/2" (range or 2 1/2?), more than 100 digits

    Ambiguous hyphens with a proper fraction are read as mixed numbers:
    "2-3/4" is 2 3/4, not the range 2 to 3/4. Results keep 2 decimals
    (2 significant digits below 1), so "1/8 tsp" becomes "0.13 tsp" even at
    factor 1.
    """
    if _NUMBER_WORD_RE.search(ingredient):
        return None
    match = _QUANTITY_RE.match(ingredient)
    if match is None:
        # No readable leading quantity: fine only if there's no number at all.
        return None if _ANY_NUMBER_RE.search(ingredient) else ingredient
    if sum(c.isdigit() for c in match.group()) > _MAX_QUANTITY_DIGITS:
        return None
    rest = ingredient[match.end():]
    if _ANY_NUMBER_RE.search(rest) or _NOT_AN_AMOUNT_RE.match(rest):
        return None
    low = _parse_number(match["low"])
    high = _parse_number(match["high"]) if match["high"] else None
    if low is None or (match["high"] and high is None):
        return None
    if high is not None and not low < high:
        return None  # "2-1 cups" is not a meaningful range
    scaled = _format_quantity(low * factor)
    if high is not None:
        scaled += match["sep"] + _format_quantity(high * factor)
    return match["lead"] + scaled + rest


def _json_number(value: Fraction) -> Union[int, float]:
    """2 -> 2, 1/2 -> 0.5: no trailing ".0" in the JSON response."""
    return value.numerator if value.denominator == 1 else float(value)


@app.get("/recipes/{recipe_id}/scaled")
def get_scaled_recipe(
    recipe_id: int,
    # Decimal, not float: the bounds are checked on the exact value, so
    # "10.0000000000000001" is rejected instead of rounding to 10.0.
    # max_digits bounds the work for inputs like "1e-999999" (still allows 1e-300).
    factor: Decimal = Query(..., gt=0, le=10, allow_inf_nan=False, max_digits=400),
):
    """Recipe with ingredient quantities multiplied by `factor` (0 < factor <= 10).

    `unscaled` lists ingredient lines that start with a quantity but were left
    as-is because the amount is ambiguous. Lines without any quantity
    ("salt to taste") are unchanged by design and are not listed.
    """
    recipe = _fetch_recipe(recipe_id)
    exact_factor = Fraction(factor)  # Decimal -> Fraction is exact: "0.1" is 1/10
    ingredients, unscaled = [], []
    # No special case for factor == 1: output format must not depend on the
    # factor ("2.0 cups" -> "2 cups" and "1/3" -> "0.33" for every factor).
    for line in recipe["ingredients"]:
        scaled = scale_ingredient(line, exact_factor)
        if scaled is None:
            unscaled.append(line)
            scaled = line
        ingredients.append(scaled)
    return {
        **recipe,
        "factor": _json_number(exact_factor),
        "ingredients": ingredients,
        "unscaled": unscaled,
    }

import atexit
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sqlite3
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

# Snapshot the real DB file (if any) before main is imported, so a test can
# prove the suite never creates or modifies it.
_REAL_DB = Path(__file__).parent / "recipes.db"


def _real_db_state():
    """(mtime, content hash) of the real DB, or None if it doesn't exist."""
    if not _REAL_DB.exists():
        return None
    return _REAL_DB.stat().st_mtime_ns, hashlib.sha256(_REAL_DB.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


_REAL_DB_STATE_BEFORE = _real_db_state()

# Point the app at a throwaway DB *before* importing main, because main
# calls init_db() at import time and would otherwise create ./recipes.db.
_IMPORT_DB_DIR = tempfile.mkdtemp()
atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, _IMPORT_DB_DIR, ignore_errors=True)

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient  # noqa: E402

import main  # noqa: E402
from main import app  # noqa: E402

client = TestClient(app)


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def temp_db(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Give every test its own empty SQLite file."""
    db_path = tmp_path / "test.db"
    monkeypatch.setattr(main, "DB_PATH", db_path)
    main.init_db()
    return db_path


def _create(ingredients, title="Test recipe", tags=None):
    r = client.post(
        "/recipes", json={"title": title, "ingredients": ingredients, "tags": tags or []}
    )
    assert r.status_code == 200
    return r.json()["id"]


def _scaled(rid, factor):
    return client.get(f"/recipes/{rid}/scaled", params={"factor": factor})


def _scale_one(ingredient, factor=2):
    """Scale a single-ingredient recipe; return (ingredients, unscaled)."""
    r = _scaled(_create([ingredient]), factor)
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    return body["ingredients"], body["unscaled"]

def test_create_and_get_recipe():
    r = client.post(

## 1. Correctness: FAIL

Prompt'taki açık kuralların hepsi karşılanıyor:
- **Factor sınırları:** Decimal ile `gt=0, le=10` kontrolü yapılıyor. 0, negatif değerler, `10.0000000000000001`, nan ve inf 422 dönüyor.
- **Kesir ve ondalık:** `1/2`, `1 1/2`, `1-1/2`, `½`, `.5` ve `0.750` doğru hesaplanıyor. Hesap `Fraction` ile tam yapılıyor.
- **Biçim:** Gereksiz sıfırlar atılıyor (2.0 yerine 2, 0.5 olarak 0.5).
- **404:** Bulunmayan tarifte dönüyor.
- **Veritabanı:** Hiç yazılmıyor, endpoint sadece okuma yapıyor.

Kabul kriterine göre FAIL sayılan şey, unscaled listesinde raporlanmadan dönen yanlış bir sayıdır. Bu tür iki durum buldum:

**a) Tireli yazılan boyut yakalanıyor ama tiresiz yazılan yakalanmıyor**
- Girdi: `"9 inch pie crust"`, factor=2
- Sonuç: `"18 inch pie crust"`, `unscaled: []`
- Neden: `_NOT_AN_AMOUNT_RE` tiresiz boyutu sadece arkasından `_CONTAINER` listesindeki bir kelime gelirse yakalıyor (`main.py:172`). "pie", "pan" ve "tortillas" bu listede yok. `"9-inch pie crust"` doğru şekilde raporlanıyor, aynı malzemenin tiresiz yazımı ise sessizce 18 inçlik tek bir kabuğa dönüşüyor.
- Aynı durum `"10 inch flour tortillas"` → `"20 inch flour tortillas"` için de geçerli. Docstring "2 inch piece" gibi tiresiz boyutların raporlandığını söylüyor.

**b) Sayı kelimesi listesi "twelve"de bitiyor**
- Girdi: `"twenty eggs"` veya `"fifteen almonds"`, factor=2
- Sonuç: satır aynen dönüyor ve `unscaled: []`
- Neden: `_NUMBER_WORD_RE` (`main.py:151-155`) sadece one…twelve, dozen, half, quarter ve third kelimelerini kapsıyor. Docstring (`main.py:238, 248`) "number words anywhere" raporlanır diyor. `"two eggs"` raporlanırken `"twenty eggs"` "miktarı olmayan malzeme" sayılıyor. Kullanıcı 2 kat tarifte "twenty eggs" görüyor ve bir uyarı almıyor.

Kabul kriterine göre FAIL sebebi olmayan, belgelenmiş sınırlamalar: `"1,5 kg"`, `"half-and-half"`, `"1/8 tsp"` sonucunun `"0.13"` olması ve `"2-3/4"` ifadesinin 2 ¾ olarak okunması.

## 2. Tests: PASS

- Prompt'taki her kural için test var:
  - factor sınırları ve geçersiz değerler: `test_invalid_factor_returns_422`, `test_factor_upper_bound_is_exact`
  - kesir, ondalık ve unicode miktarlar: `test_scaling_values`
  - miktarı olmayan malzemeler: `test_ingredients_without_quantity_unchanged_and_not_flagged`
  - gereksiz sıfırlar: `test_factor_is_echoed_without_trailing_zeros`
  - 404: `test_scaled_unknown_recipe_404`
- Uç değerler kapsanmış: 0, -0, 1e-300, 10, 10'u az geçen değerler, 5000 basamaklı sayılar ve ters aralıklar.
- Geçici veritabanı doğru kurulmuş: `main` import edilmeden önce `RECIPE_BOX_DB` ortam değişkeni ayarlanıyor ve her test için `tmp_path` kullanılıyor.
- `test_tests_do_not_use_real_db` gerçek `recipes.db` dosyasının mtime ve hash değerinin değişmediğini kontrol ediyor.
- Orijinal verinin değişmediği hem API'den hem de doğrudan SQL ile kontrol ediliyor (`test_scaling_does_not_modify_original`).

Eksik testler:
- `"9 inch pie crust"` ve `"10 inch flour tortillas"` (tiresiz boyut, container olmadan). Yukarıdaki 1a hatasını yakalardı.
- `"twenty eggs"` ve `"fifteen almonds"` (twelve'den büyük sayı kelimeleri). 1b hatasını yakalardı.
- Kesirli bir malzemenin 1'den küçük factor ile çarpılması, örneğin `"1/3 cup"` × 0.5 → `"0.17 cup"`. Şu anki testlerde kesirli malzemeler hep 1 veya daha büyük factor ile deneniyor.

## 3. Clarity: PASS

- İsimler anlaşılır: `_NOT_AN_AMOUNT_RE`, `_ANY_NUMBER_RE`, `_parse_number`, `_format_quantity`.
- Regex'ler ve kararlar yorumlarla açıklanmış.
- Hata yönetimi açık: `None` "güvenle ölçeklenemez" anlamına geliyor ve satır `unscaled` listesine ekleniyor.
- Küçük bir not: endpoint docstring'i (`main.py:303-305`) güncel değil. "`unscaled` lists ingredient lines that start with a quantity" diyor, ama bu round'dan sonra `"flour 200 g"`, `"two eggs"` ve `"V8 juice"` gibi baştan miktarla başlamayan satırlar da listeleniyor. Bu metin OpenAPI dokümanında da görünüyor. Bu tek başına FAIL için yeterli değil, ama düzeltilmesi iyi olur.

VERDICT: REVISE
